Industry News: Drinks You Can Make By The Batch

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1602 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holiday magic is a lot of unpaid labor in an ugly Christmas sweater.
  • In a recent development, these punches, pitchers and alcohol-free drinks are perfect for pre-initiative prepping.There’s a spicy margarita you can carry in the tequila bottle, a pear punch for the fancy friends, and a peppermint espresso martini you can make for 16.
  • Julie Reiner, co-founder of Brooklyn’s Clover Club, served punch and freezer cocktails at a Halloween party for 20.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bring something good. Let the grown-ups serve themselves.

Holiday magic is a lot of unpaid labor in an ugly Christmas sweater. Between class potlucks, Thanksgiving logistics and buying the only bread your kid will eat, you’ve got enough on your plate. Now add holiday parties, questionable white elephant gifts and 400 things to do before the doorbell rings. The last thing you need is a second job as a bartender.

In a recent development, these punches, pitchers and alcohol-free drinks are perfect for pre-initiative prepping.There’s a spicy margarita you can carry in the tequila bottle, a pear punch for the fancy friends, and a peppermint espresso martini you can make for 16. Some need a little attention before serving. Most are ready to pour once chilled.

Julie Reiner, co-founder of Brooklyn’s Clover Club, served punch and freezer cocktails at a Halloween party for 20. “The goal is to spend time with your guests, not be stuck behind the bar all night!” she said.

According to recent reports, A little planning helps. Julianna McIntosh, the cocktail creator behind Join Jules, recommends using fresh citrus the day of your party and accounting for the water normally added when you shake or stir a drink with ice. Hannah Chamberlain, the recipe developer behind Spirited LA, has another rule: Hold the ice and bubbly until guests arrive. Otherwise, you risk a watered-down punch with flat bubbles.

It has been revealed that bringing a batch to someone else’s party? Pack it in a tightly sealed container, keep it chilled and add the bubbles when you arrive. Then pour yourself a glass and let someone else worry about the rest.

Bitter, bubbly and ridiculously easy to scale up. Natalie Migliarini, the cocktail creator behind Beautiful Booze, makes her Negroni Sbagliato with equal parts Select Aperitivo, sweet vermouth and prosecco, finished with an orange slice. The recipe makes one, but you can multiply the aperitivo and vermouth to serve your group, then chill them together in a bottle. When it's time to drink, pour over ice, add the prosecco and stir. No shaker required.

Get the recipe at Beautiful Booze.

Everyone’s due at six. The first guest rings the bell at 5:42. Have Reiner’s Boat House Punch ready. Gin, Aperol, St-Germain and three citrus juices get a bright, bittersweet lift from sparkling rosé. “I always want my punch to be a crowd-pleaser, but it needs to have a little personality too!” Reiner noted. This makes a substantial batch, so save it for a crowd. Let the lemon peels and sugar sit for at least an hour or overnight, and freeze a large ice block ahead of time. Add the ice and rosé just before serving.

Get the recipe at Cocktails Distilled.

According to recent reports, champagne tastes even better when nobody has to mix 12 individual cocktails. Chamberlain's large-batch take on the French 75 combines gin, fresh lemon, orange bitters and homemade cranberry-ginger syrup, then gets topped with sparkling wine. It serves six to eight and looks impressive without requiring an elaborate garnish situation. Make the syrup ahead and chill the ingredients. When guests arrive, add large ice cubes and the bubbly, give it a stir, and you're done. If the finished punch tastes a little dull, Chamberlain recommends adding a few dashes of Angostura or cardamom bitters to give it more personality.

According to recent reports, love your friends. Not enough to muddle each of them a mojito. Averie Sunshine’s pomegranate mojito punch at Averie Cooks combines white rum, mint, pomegranate juice and seeds, lemon and sparkling water in one pitcher. It makes four generous drinks, so double it for a bigger gathering. Chill the liquids ahead, then muddle the mint and assemble the punch just before serving so the leaves stay fresh, and the bubbles don't disappear. Ice goes in the glasses. One round of muddling. Everybody gets a drink.

Get the recipe at Averie Cooks.

In a recent development, here, Chamberlain pairs pear nectar with gin, ginger liqueur, rosemary syrup, lemon, cardamom bitters and dry bubbly in her Calling Card Punch. It's an elegant, herbal alternative to the usual holiday punch and serves six to eight. Make the rosemary syrup ahead, chill the ingredients and add the sparkling wine while serving.

“I tend to build my punch a little less sweet and then I’ll often have a little extra syrup I can add if it seems unbalanced,” Chamberlain noted. It's easier to add sweetness than take it away.

By the time dessert rolls around, the adults deserve something stronger than another cup of coffee. McIntosh combines vodka, espresso or cold brew, coffee liqueur and peppermint syrup for a holiday spin on the espresso martini. Her large-batch version makes about 16 servings, with no individual shaking required. Mix everything ahead, chill it in the freezer for about two hours and give it a quick whirl in the blender if you want that signature foam. Pour into a punch bowl and let everyone help themselves. Crushed candy cane rims are optional. You've already done enough decorating.

Recent findings suggest that give the alcohol-free drinks their own spot at the party. America’s Test Kitchen combines cranberries, ginger, rosemary, cinnamon and star anise in a sweetened base you can make up to four days ahead. When guests arrive, add chilled cranberry juice, orange juice and seltzer. It makes 16 servings, enough for an open house where another family keeps appearing in the doorway.

Get the recipe at America’s Test Kitchen.

Industry observers note that the tiny apple leaves are optional – you have enough crafts coming home from school. Chamberlain’s Fallen Leaves Punch mixes cognac, tart apple cider and lemon with homemade cranberry-cinnamon syrup for eight servings. It's a good Friendsgiving option if you want something tart, fruity and a little stronger than cider.

“In terms of flavor combinations, it’s hard to disappoint with the combination of seasonal spice and fruit,” Chamberlain stated. Make the syrup ahead, squeeze the lemons the day of and stir everything over a large ice block at serving.

Taco night doesn’t need a November makeover. McIntosh makes six spicy margaritas right in the tequila bottle, giving you a batch and a carrying container in one. You'll need to pour out some tequila first; the recipe tells you how much. Mix everything in the bottle, then let it sit in the freezer for 2 to 4 hours, then pour it over ice into salt-rimmed glasses. All the fun of margaritas without anyone spending the evening squeezing limes.

According to recent reports, apple cider is doing a lot of heavy lifting this holiday season, let it have some rum. Chamberlain's Cider Rum Punch combines tart cider, aged pineapple rum, lemon, orange bitters and a homemade mulling-spice syrup for six servings. She makes it every year, and it's easy to see why. The warm spices play nicely with the fruit without turning the whole thing into a scented candle. Make the syrup ahead, then combine everything in a pitcher with plenty of ice and stir until chilled. Bonus: There's no sparkling wine to worry about going flat.

The kids’ table and Grandma can drink from the same pitcher. McIntosh’s pineapple passion fruit agua fresca blends tropical fruit, lime and agave into six refreshing alcohol-free servings. Frozen passion fruit pulp works, and there are no bubbles to go flat on the drive. Make it up to two days ahead, refrigerate and give it a good stir before pouring over ice.

According to recent reports, after the holiday lights walk, everyone comes home freezing and suddenly needs something warm RIGHT NOW. Sunshine's peppermint white hot chocolate at Averie Cooks combines milk, melted white chocolate and a little peppermint extract. The recipe makes five mugs, but you can easily double or triple it for a houseful of cold kids and grown-ups. Heat everything together over low heat, stirring until the chocolate melts. Don't let it boil, and go easy on the peppermint. A little goes a long way. Add marshmallows if you've got them. Nobody's going to complain.

Get the recipe at Averie Cooks.

The wine people and the margarita people can share a pitcher. Migliarini’s tequila sangria at Beautiful Booze combines Sauvignon Blanc with tequila, cranberry syrup, fresh cranberries, red and green apples and lime. “Keeping it simple, my recipe includes fruits that are available throughout the entire year,” she writes in the recipe. It serves five to six, making it a good choice for a casual Friendsgiving. Chill the wine, tequila and fruit mixture ahead, then add the lemon-lime soda just before serving.

Get the recipe at Beautiful Booze.

No fish. Promise. Amy Traynor’s Fish House Punch at Moody Mixologist combines cognac and aged rum with peach liqueur, lemon and cold black tea. Think peach iced tea with considerably more going on. Her recipe includes a version for 10, so there's no need to multiply or do any guesswork. Freeze a large ice block ahead, stir the ingredients over it at serving and finish each glass with freshly grated nutmeg. Fair warning: This one's boozy.

Get the recipe at Moody Mixologist.

Recent findings suggest that dinner’s over, the kids have claimed the television and nobody’s ready to leave. Put a pot of McIntosh’s mulled Aperol on the stove for the spritz drinkers still on your sofa. Dry white wine, Aperol, apple cider and honey warm with orange and whole spices. It makes six servings and needs just 15 to 20 minutes over low heat. Don't let it boil. Ladle into mugs and let everyone settle in. The kitchen will smell like you had a proposal.

Just one of the Boys raising two girls.

AJ McLean, the singer, songwriter, and most tattooed member of The Backstreet Boys just moved his family to Fresh York City. “All three of the ladies in my life love New York,” he states — and he’s all about it. “Celebrating Christmas in New York this year is going to be fantastic.”.

Recent findings suggest that but before he can take the family to the Rockettes, McLean has an album to launch (Sex, Love, and Music, out Nov. 27) and a solo tour to rock (The Better Man Tour). He is also busy as the spokesman for Delsym 12-Hour Cough Relief, which he notes saved a performance during The Backstreet Boys residency at The Sphere last year. McLean took a break from his tour to take Fatherly’s Cool Dad questionnaire — and talk about staying healthy, sober, and putting family first.

I think I am a cool dad. I think I'm a cool dad because I really kind of let my kids form their own opinions and have a voice, and we work as a team. I want my girls to always have a voice. That's super key to me. Sometimes, they have too much of a voice, but it's OK. That's when dad has to step in and reel it back a little bit. I want my girls to just always look up to their dad, and I try to set the best example that I can.

AJ McLean on his solo “The Better Man” Tour.

What's the best film to watch with kids?

It has been revealed that so I'm an ’80s kid and I am so happy that I turned my girls onto Labyrinth, which they absolutely love; The Goonies, which they absolutely love; and Gremlins. They are obsessed, especially with Labyrinth. When I mentioned it to them, they were a little hesitant, and then once we watched it, I went back to work and caught wind from the wife that they've watched it repeatedly days after, and I'm like, "Yes, I did it.".

What's one thing you wish your kids had today that you had growing up, especially as a kid from the ’80s?

I wish they had cassette tape players. I did get a cassette tape player gift box from my boys over at Aerosmith, and it came with a cassette tape of their new album — it was a promotional thing. And I highlighted it to my daughters, and they did not know what they were looking at. They put it in backwards. I'm like, "No, no, no, no, no, no." And then they were like, "What is the red button?" I noted, "No, that's for recording." And they were astounded when I pressed play and this little speaker was playing and I'm like, "When your dad was growing up, that was it. That's all we had. There was no Bose surround sound, there was none of that.".

And then my youngest — last year as a birthday present from one of her friends — got a Discman. And she of course put the CD in upside down, I had to show her the right way. That was painful. But she really loves her freaking Discman. She loves it. And I love that they're starting to come back where you actually have to buy the CD. I keep telling my girls, "There's pictures in there; there's thank yous; there's a whole thing. It's not just listening to the music; it's a whole package deal, where you don't get that if you're listening to iTunes. You see one picture and listen to the music, that's it. Albums were a thing." So I'm starting to get them into that now, which I really love.

What's music have you successfully introduced your kids to?

My oldest daughter's first album was The Beatles’ White Album. She learned every word between the ages of 2 and 3. And she was a sponge. My wife is the biggest Beatles fan out of anyone I've ever met in my life. She is diehard. So that was her first album. She's like, "This is what my kids are listening to, Beatles." I'm like, "OK.".

AJ McLean and his family, pictured here in 2022, recently moved to New York City.

And what music have your kids introduced you to?

Sources indicate that recently, I took the family to the premiere of Michael, and my daughters knew who Michael Jackson was, but after the film, the obsession was over the top. They know songs I've never heard, deep cuts. People forget about Michael's Jackson’s Xscape album and they're saying, "Dad, play such and such a song." And I'm like, "That's not a song." They're like, "Yes, it is." They know more music, I think, now than I've ever known in my entire life. We have a very musical family, very musical family.

What does fatherhood mean to you in the current world?

Fatherhood, to me, means protection. It means compassion, understanding. It means listening with my ears and not my mouth, and being nonjudgmental, which I'm a very nonjudgmental person anyways, but just by nature, that's how I was raised. And trying to really broaden my daughters’ spectrum of the world, and to love everyone, and to accept everyone, and to be colorblind, to be genderblind, to be just very open and loving. And they are. They are two of the coolest kids I think any father could ever ask for. They are super smart. They are loving kids. They are people, people like me.

They're not shy by any means. They will talk to everybody and talk their ear off, and I have no idea where they get that from. But yeah, I try to just really set an example, especially as a father and as a man, I want my daughters to look at me and then be able to say when the time comes that they want to date boys, this is what a boy should be. This is what a man should be, like, respectful. And I grew up single-parent household, so I grew up to very much so respect women to the utmost, and put them up on a pedestal, which it's kind of a give and take, but to really know that none of us would be here without a woman, let's just say that.

Sources indicate that what piece of clothing or gear are you really passionate about right now? What do you can't get enough of?

It has been revealed that I mean, I'm a sneakerhead. I have a problem. And I've gotten my girls into it now, which my wife is so thrilled about.

Well, it's easier for me because I'm done. My foot's where it's at, it ain't going up, it ain't going down, but my daughters are still growing. So when I go get a pair of Jordans that are like $200 and then my kids want to match daddy's shoes, it's a little like they're going to be in them for six months and then they're going to be out of them. But then we donate them anyway, so we're not just throwing them out; we're donating them.

What are you wearing right now then? What's on your feet?

Right now, I've got my travel shoes, which are my Adidas Ultraboost, but my everyday shoes are [Jordan] 1s or 3s. That is my go-to. My collection has gotten pretty large. And my daughters now, they're nowhere near as many as me, but they're starting to catch up.

What does Rochelle love about you?

Sources indicate that I think she loves my heart, my generosity, my kindness, my ability to be very comforting and loving. I'm a very affectionate person. I try to be a very loyal person. I try to be a very honest person. I have my faults; nobody's perfect. I tell people I'm perfectly imperfect. And I think she just loves me for me. I think even more so now, being sober for over five years and living my true authentic self, our relationship now I think is the best it's ever been, being in each other's lives for 15 years.

We went through some tough stuff. We separated, we were living separately, and we both now can look back and reflect on what needed to happen. There are no mistakes. I believe everything happens exactly how it's meant to be. We needed that time apart to grow individually and to grow as a unit. And now, we're living together as a family for the first time in almost four years. We're renting a place in New York so my girls can go to an incredible dance school, and all three of the ladies in my life love New York, and they would've moved there years ago.

In a recent development, they're having the time of their life. And I told them, because we actually moved the tail end of summer, and none of my girls have ever experienced humidity or the heat that is the East Coast.

And I would FaceTime them and be like, "Oh, dear God, what's with your hair?" But now they understand.

Now they know that everyone leaves the city in the summer, so you'll do that next year.

It has been revealed that exactly. But celebrating Christmas in New York this year is going to be fantastic.

So I just got over a cold myself, and it's like, I'm wondering, you're touring, you moved, you travel, you're now in crowded Latest York, and you have germy kids. Is this why you partnered with Delsym: 12-Hour Cough Relief? How do you deal with the illness, staying healthy, prevention and all that.

I mean, it's pretty crazy because after doing what I do for ... I've been in the business for 40 years. That is how long I've been in the world of entertainment. And I think especially with being with the Boys, my immunity has kind of skyrocketed because of, I think, how much interaction I have with people, but I'm human, and I still do get sick. It's rare, but it does happen, especially being out here on my own. I don't have the boys to lean on. If I go down, I go down. And this is cold and flu season right now, and you're on a tight quarters on a bus. If somebody gets sick, it spreads like wildfire. But for me, two years ago when we first kicked off our residency at Sphere, the second weekend, I got very sick and I was coughing uncontrollably, and that's not an easy show to do if you're not well.

According to recent reports, and Delsym is the only product I know works 100%. It's 12 hours of relief that not only does it get me through the show, but it continues after that, because that's really where you feel it. If you're not in a good way, not only are you going to feel it during the show, but afterwards because you're pushing through. But that is my go-to, has been, will always be. Moving forward as an artist, that, I know is my guarantee to get through a show because let's face it, nobody wants to go see a concert and watch their artist cough more than sing, you know what I mean? And especially me out here by myself.

Here you’ll find a curated list of mom-owned stores and businesses you’ll want to experience first hand.

In a recent development, you’ve likely seen them, and even likely shopped with them: They’re local (and yes, sometimes national) mom-owned stores, popups or small businesses. You want to support them cause, well, they’re your fellow moms, but you’re also busy so cutting through the noise and helping you choose where to spend your hard-earned dollars is paramount.

The Very Best Gifts For Dads 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • From a cashmere blazer suitable for any occasion to smart tools that’ll make his life easier, these gifts are sure to suit anyone on your list.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From a cashmere blazer suitable for any occasion to smart tools that’ll make his life easier, these gifts are sure to suit anyone on your list.

They say that shopping for dads is difficult. We ask: How so? We are a demographic that is easy to flatter and easy to please. If you think of us enough to buy us something, you’re 90% of the way there. And that last 10%? OK, that’s the tough part. How do you get us a gift that is unique and useful, something we’ll not just like but actually love? You’ve come to the right place.

Sources indicate that for our 2026 list of the best gifts for dads, we’ve curated products that we know and love, ones we can say with confidence stand out from the rest of the pack. And yeah, there are a few things on this list that we just think are cool — because why not? We guarantee you’ll find something here to make him — or yourself — smile, smell good, look good, or feel cool.

According to recent reports, every product you see here is independently selected by our editors, writers, and experts. If you click a link on our site and buy something, we may earn an affiliate commission.

A dull knife is a dangerous knife. This two-sided cylindrical sharpener is a great way to keep your blades in working order. Secure your knife at the correct angle with the included magnetic holder and roll the cylinder — which has two sides, one meant for blade sharpening and one meant for honing — back and forth against the knife’s edge. Simple. Effective. The kit comes with a sharpener, strop, magnetic holder, and a display.

Recent findings suggest that A baseball cap can do more than cover up a missed shower. Siegelman Stable makes the sort you put on deliberately. The New York label has fans like Knicks star Jalen Brunson, but there's nothing shouty about its classic shape and embroidered logo. Wear it with a jacket that fits and sneakers that aren't falling apart, and suddenly school pickup doesn't look like the end of a very long day.

A cashmere blazer sounds like the sort of thing you wear to complain about the service on a yacht. This one is more useful. Quince cuts it from 100 percent Mongolian cashmere, then adds horn buttons and a partial lining for just enough structure. It wears like a sweater but looks like he made an effort. Throw it over a T-shirt and he's ready for dinner without having to change into something stiff.

In a recent development, there are pants that look good and pants you can comfortably wear on a six-hour flight. Vuori's Meta Pant manages both. The classic five-pocket silhouette looks polished enough for the office or dinner, but the four-way stretch, moisture-wicking fabric, and quick-drying finish make them considerably more forgiving than ordinary trousers. The straight-leg fit leaves room through the hips and thighs without looking baggy.

One pair of boots for a rainy commute, a weekend away, and dinner somewhere nice. That's the argument for Blundstone's Heritage #156. Premium black leather keeps them sharp, cushioned footbeds and cork filler make them increasingly comfortable, and Goodyear welt construction means the soles can be replaced. They don't need babying or a special outfit. A rare thing: shoes that get more useful as they get older.

Vitamix, the most storied brand in blenders, is becoming a bit more portable. The fresh Nano blends two 20-ounce cups — complete with travel lids — so that you can make a smoothie in the morning, saving your substantial, overpowered Vitamix for more heavy-duty food prep.

According to recent reports, A man's wallet shouldn't resemble a filing cabinet. Bellroy's Hide & Seek keeps things slim without forcing him to give up cash, cards, or the occasional receipt he's convinced he'll need someday. Made from supple leather, the classic bifold has five card slots, a bill compartment, and concealed pockets for anything he'd rather keep tucked away. The Everglade green is particularly good, a welcome departure from the usual black and brown.

Sources indicate that men's jewelry doesn't have to involve leather cords, nautical hardware, or anything resembling a guitar pick. Mejuri's Braided Curb Chain Bracelet keeps things simple, with interwoven stainless-steel links and a sleek platinum-colored finish. It has enough presence to look intentional without becoming the centerpiece of his outfit. Water-resistant and durable enough for everyday wear, it works equally well with a T-shirt or a tailored jacket.

Ian McEwan’s latest novel proves this is the golden age for sci-fi dystopian. While the flooded, fragmented future laid out in the book shows 2119 to be a bit of a horror show, the scholars reminiscence for art, love, and lost chance in 2014 is equal parts chilling, moving, and full of hope. .

Steve McQueen wore Persol 714s. That's a pretty compelling endorsement, even six decades later. The Italian-made frames fold into a compact shape, with rich acetate and discreet metal detailing that have survived more fashion cycles than most sunglasses ever will. No oversize logos, no aggressive wraparound lenses. Just an excellent pair of shades for a man whose taste hasn't been entirely surrendered to practical footwear.

In a recent development, some coffee-table books are glorified furniture. This one earns its space. Architectural Digest at 100 opens the doors to a century of remarkable homes, from those of David Bowie and Truman Capote to Barack and Michelle Obama. You'll also find work by Frank Lloyd Wright, Frank Gehry, and other design heavyweights. The photography is gorgeous, but the real draw is seeing how people with extraordinary taste actually lived. For the dad who notices the architecture before he notices the menu.

Yes, it's a notebook. A very good one. Leuchtturm1917 gives him 251 numbered pages, a table of contents, two ribbon markers, and binding that lies flat without a wrestling match. It's the place for the business idea, the sketch, the travel blueprint, or the novel he's been threatening to write. No apps, passwords, or notifications. Just paper substantial enough to make him want to use it.

The Sabah lives in the sweet spot between a loafer and a slipper, without looking much like either. Handmade in Turkey, the Blackout version pairs soft black leather with hand stitching, a leather insole that shapes to his foot, and a replaceable rubber outsole. Wear it with trousers, shorts or whatever passes for his weekend uniform. It's the sort of relaxed, distinctive shoe you notice precisely because it isn't trying so hard.

Industry observers note that most headphones are anonymous plastic. Nothing's Headphone (1) Pro looks like someone actually thought about the design. Behind the striking shell are three drivers, adaptive noise cancellation, and tuning developed with Metropolis Studios. Real buttons and dials mean less fumbling at the earcups, while the battery runs up to 68 hours with noise cancellation off. For a dad who's spent enough time listening to other people's playlists, here's a way back to his own.

It has a tuning dial. An actual dial. Tivoli's Model One is a gorgeous antidote to the idea that every piece of technology needs an app and a setup tutorial. The wood cabinet, simple knobs, and traditional AM/FM radio make it a pleasure to use, while Bluetooth is there when he wants to stream something. Set it on a desk or bookshelf. Turn it on. Listen. Remember when that was all it took?

Marshall's Minor IV earbuds have a little of the brand's old-school amplifier swagger, minus the equipment truck. The black-and-gold finish is sharp, the angled design is made for a comfortable fit, and touch controls handle music and calls. Battery life runs up to seven hours per charge and more than 30 with the case. They're water-resistant, too. A solid upgrade for the dad who still cares what comes through his headphones, even if he now listens at a more reasonable volume.

If he has opinions about beans, water temperature, and extraction times, he needs a grinder that can keep up. Fellow's Opus 2 handles everything from espresso to cold brew, with fine grind adjustments and 48-millimeter conical burrs. Anti-static technology cuts down on the mess, and magnetic catch cups make switching methods simple. The sleek profile doesn't hurt. But the point isn't the countertop aesthetic. It's better coffee before any guests start asking where their shoes are.

Recent findings suggest that this year’s Booker prize winner is a dystopian sci-fi satire that takes place up and down the British coast. It’s not exactly a beach read, but a novel that is a perfectly odd reflection of our perfectly strange times.

It has been revealed that A slab of teak isn't an obvious gift until you see this one. Sonder LA's Bradbury board has three compartments for chopped ingredients or a serious cheese spread. Turn it over and a deep groove catches up to 4.5 ounces of carving juices, saving the counter from the aftermath of Sunday dinner. Heavy, handsome, and useful enough to leave out all the time. It's the cutting board version of buying one good thing instead of three mediocre ones.

Smithey's cast-iron chef skillet looks like something a grandparent might have handed down, except this one comes ready to start its own history. The polished interior develops seasoning over time, the curved sides make tossing food easier, and the weight holds heat beautifully for searing. It's made in South Carolina and looks good enough to bring straight to the table. For the dad who finds chopping onions therapeutic and considers a well-seasoned pan a point of pride.

A drawer full of knives is no substitute for one excellent one. Made In's 8-inch chef knife is forged in Thiers, France, by a fifth-generation bladesmith, with a full-tang construction that gives it balance and control. It can mince herbs, chop vegetables, and tackle the Sunday roast without switching tools. The best part is how often he'll use it. Unlike most expensive kitchen gifts, this won't spend its life on display.

Finding a night when everyone's free is now the hardest part of poker. Mark & Graham takes care of everything else: two decks of cards, 100 chips, and a pebbled-leather case lined in suede. It's compact enough to put away but handsome enough not to. Add a monogram if he likes that sort of thing. Then put an evening on the calendar and let him spend a few hours with people who don't need help finding their cleats.

Recent findings suggest that no sprawling backyard? No problem. Solo Stove's Mesa XL brings a real flame to a compact tabletop fire pit, with an airflow system that helps keep smoke down. The stainless-steel body looks good on a patio, and the setup is simple enough for an impromptu evening outside. Roast marshmallows with the kids or pull up chairs after bedtime. It's a small fire with an outsized ability to make an ordinary Tuesday feel like something else.

Recent findings suggest that the mind of the famous neurologist Oliver Sacks was like no other. His letters show his thoughts in full light — restless, deep, and full of love and wisdom. Think of this book as competency porn — a counter to the daily doomscrolling.

Chess is a wonderful game, provided you enjoy being intellectually humiliated by a 12-year-old. This smart chessboard might help him even the odds. Built-in sensors track every move, while LED lights suggest what to do next, and AI-powered coaching helps players improve without enduring another smug lecture about strategy. Connect it to Chess.com or Lichess to challenge opponents around the world, play against the computer, or settle a family rivalry the old-fashioned way.

It has been revealed that A puffer jacket for your neck sounds ridiculous until the temperature drops. Cotopaxi's Fuego Down Scarf delivers the warmth of an insulated jacket in a lightweight, packable scarf, with responsibly sourced down, a water-resistant recycled nylon shell, and bold color-blocked stripes. A pull-through slit keeps it securely in place, while pockets at either end give Dad somewhere to warm his hands when gloves aren't enough.

Recent findings suggest that A leisurely hike is one thing. Scrambling up a rocky trail and navigating a steep descent is another. Leki's Makalu Cork Lite trekking poles give Dad some extra stability when the terrain gets tricky, without weighing him down. Made from lightweight aluminum, each pole weighs less than 9 ounces and has an ergonomic cork grip that absorbs moisture and gradually conforms to his hand. Adjustable locking mechanisms make it easy to change the length on the go, while carbide tips provide traction on uneven ground. They telescope down for packing, too.

Industry observers note that the nightstand looks like a cable graveyard. Anker's MagStand gives it a chance at redemption, charging three devices with a magnetic pad for compatible iPhones, a retractable USB-C cable, and another USB-C port. A small display reveals charging status and other information, while a quieter overnight mode suits a bedroom. It's the sort of unglamorous upgrade that feels extremely glamorous the first time he reaches for a fully charged phone and doesn't pull a nest of wires off the table.

According to recent reports, for the Formula 1 dad with extremely confident opinions about tire strategy. Logitech's McLaren racing bundle pairs an F1-style wheel with direct-drive force feedback, so the steering pushes back as traction and cornering forces change in the game. It's far closer to a simulator than a standard controller, and requires the space and enthusiasm to match. A serious indulgence, yes. But probably less expensive than any other way of letting him pretend he's on the grid.

It has been revealed that at some point in your parenting adventures, whether you like it or not, you will have to face the trials and tribulations of what it means to be a teenager. This book deeply, and sometimes even profoundly, explores just this, with equal parts science and storytelling, it might not help you truly prepare for your little one to hit their pubescence, but it will give you empathy and maybe even a bit of appreciation.

Keys jangle, scratch phones, and vanish precisely when everyone is late. Orbitkey stacks three to seven of them inside a slim leather organizer, then adds a tracker that works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub on compatible devices. It takes less room in a pocket and looks considerably better than a bulky ring. Not the showiest gift here. Possibly the one he'll use most often.

Sources indicate that remember when listening to music meant putting on an album and actually listening to the whole thing? The Retradisc CD player brings back that pleasure, minus the tangled headphone cords. Its transparent case lets Dad watch his CDs spin, while Bluetooth connectivity lets him pair it with wireless headphones or speakers. There's also a traditional headphone jack, anti-skip protection, and a rechargeable battery.

Some dads count steps. Others count elevation gain. Garmin's Enduro 4 is for the second group, with trail maps, endurance metrics, stamina tracking, and more than 100 activity profiles. Its solar-assisted battery can last up to 90 days in smartwatch mode under Garmin's specified sunlight conditions, which makes it especially useful on long trips. It's overkill for walking the dog. For someone planning his next ultramarathon before finishing the last one, that's the appeal.

He tracks workouts, sleep, and maybe his resting heart rate. Why stop at weight? Withings' BodyScan 2 measures composition by body region, tracks muscle and fat mass, and offers cardiovascular metrics including a six-lead ECG and vascular age estimates. Results appear on a screen built into the handle. Some advanced analysis requires a subscription, and it's not a replacement for a doctor. Buy it for the data enthusiast who actually wants this information, not as a hint that somebody should get in shape.

The fleece vest has spent far too long being associated with finance bros who say things like “let's circle back.” It's time to reclaim it. The North Face's Glacier Vest is lightweight, warm, and made entirely from recycled polyester fleece. It's the ideal extra layer for chilly morning walks, weekend hikes, or an office where someone has apparently mistaken the thermostat for a refrigerator dial.

Because exercise equipment has a way of proliferating and is generally ugly, at-home workouts tend to require a sacrifice of one kind or another. The possible lone exception is the rowing machine: Rowing works 86 percent of the body’s muscles and can be as cardio-intense (or mellow) as you like, while improving joint flexibility. One of the newest and sleekest rowing machines, the Ergatta uses actual water resistance, which makes it as effective as it is quiet (as well as cool-looking, with its transparent reservoir). It’s got all the fitness potential of a traditional rowing machine, but packaged with cutting-edge, immersive technology (a reasonable $29/month) that keeps monotony at bay. The jewel in the crown, though, is its design: Handmade of cherry wood, it's the farthest thing from an eyesore, and it can be folded up and stowed away, so it works in even the tiniest of homes.

Just looking at this hammock drops your diastolic blood pressure. String this version up between two trees, or on a stand, and the generous 55-by-82-inch hammock will cradle him with an open back that prevents sweating in the summer heat. The cord is as soft as cotton, but the synthetic blend inhibits discoloration in the sun, is anti-microbial, and easy to clean with soap and water when the kids spill watermelon on it.

Sure, you can find a dozen pricey, aesthetically arresting turntables out there, but for the man who actually listens to his records, you can't beat AudioTechnica. The biggest upgrade for a vinyl spin is found in the manual turntable and the seemingly no-frills AT-LPW30 puts all the focus on great sound and proper listening experience.

He may be shaving in a hurry, but the products don't have to feel like a compromise. Le Labo pairs a rich shaving cream with a soothing after-shave balm in minimalist aluminum tubes. Bergamot, lavender, violet, and tonka bean give the set a distinctive scent without the usual blast of drugstore aftershave. It turns a boring morning task into something a little more civilized. No 10-step ritual required.

Industry observers note that A beautiful latest edition of William Gibson's seminal 1984 cyberpunk novel. Illustrated throughout by Anna Mill, with a handsome slipcase.

Aventus is not a subtle little stocking stuffer. It's Creed's substantial, unapologetically luxurious fragrance, with fresh bergamot and blackcurrant giving way to pineapple, pink pepper, and smoky birch. The mix feels rich without veering into syrupy. Yes, the price is extravagant. That's rather the point. For a dad who's particular about fragrance and rarely buys the expensive bottle for himself, this is a proper splurge.

Industry observers note that if the household has a snorer, a restless sleeper, or a neighbor who enjoys late-night construction projects, these might be the most welcome gift of the season. Ozlo's Sleepbuds 2 sit low in the ear, including for side sleepers, and play sleep sounds to help mask noise. They can also stream music or podcasts, with up to 14 hours of battery life and a private in-ear alarm. The case monitors bedroom conditions, too. They can't make anyone sleep later. They might make the hours he gets a little quieter.

Dad's face has been through a lot. Early mornings, late nights, questionable sleep, and possibly decades of washing it with whatever soap happens to be in the shower. It deserves better. Caldera + Lab's The Regimen gives him a proper skin care routine without requiring a degree in dermatology. The four-piece set includes a gentle exfoliating cleanser, a botanical serum, a daily moisturizer, and an eye treatment designed to tackle the appearance of puffiness and dark circles.

Some people throw out a broken gadget. Others want to see exactly what's gone wrong inside. iFixit's Mako kit is for the latter, with 64 precision bits for laptops, game consoles, phones, and the obscure screws that defeat an ordinary screwdriver. The aluminum driver has a magnetic socket and swivel top; the case keeps everything from scattering across the table. A small, deeply satisfying gift for the dad who believes almost anything deserves one attempt at repair.

The moment you become a dad, people start assuming you can fix things. Leatherman's Wingman won't supply the expertise, but it gives him 14 ways to look prepared. Spring-action pliers, scissors, screwdrivers, wire cutters, a blade, and a package opener all fold into one pocketable tool. The knife opens with one hand and the 25-year warranty suggests it's meant to stick around. One of those gifts he'll reach for long after the holidays are forgotten.

In a recent development, flat-pack furniture has destroyed more relationships than anyone cares to admit. Hoto's PivotDrive won't save a marriage, but it might prevent an argument over a bookshelf. This sleek cordless screwdriver has a head that pivots 90 degrees, with four locking positions to reach screws buried in tight corners and awkward spaces. Five torque settings, two speeds, and 16 interchangeable bits handle everything from furniture assembly to minor household repairs. It's a clever upgrade for the guy who enjoys fixing things almost as much as complaining about how badly they were designed.

Industry News: Ten Deaths & 5,400 Cases Later, The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles Elimination Status

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a subgroup of the World Health Organization, will make the official announcement today.
  • Measles has made headlines time and time again over the past two years, as cases have hit record highs and vaccination rates have reached record lows.
  • The group is expected to make a formal announcement today.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a subgroup of the World Health Organization, will make the official announcement today.

Measles has made headlines time and time again over the past two years, as cases have hit record highs and vaccination rates have reached record lows. Now, the looming threat has come true: according to sources familiar with the vote, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) revoked the United States’ measles elimination status.

The group is expected to make a formal announcement today.

Industry observers note that to date, the U.S. has racked up more than 5,400 confirmed measles cases in 2026, the most to be reported in the United States in 35 years. There have been 10 reported measles-related deaths so far, including an infant in Wisconsin earlier this month. Measles was considered officially eliminated in the U.S. in 2000, meaning there had been no large outbreaks or uncontrolled domestic transmission of the virus for at least 12 months prior.

According to recent reports, america’s current measles outbreaks first began in January 2025 in West Texas. By January 2026, the spread continued unchecked. PAHO’s meeting to discuss the country’s measles elimination status was originally scheduled for April 2026, KFF reports, but the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) asked for more time to determine whether measles cases were being transmitted domestically or “imported” (for example, if someone contracted measles abroad and then brought it to the U.S.). According to NBC, measles is now considered endemic to the U.S.

Recent findings suggest that many challenges have contributed to the country’s ongoing measles outbreaks, from sweeping funding and staffing cuts to public health agencies to a lack of leadership — there was no Senate-confirmed director of the CDC for an entire year during this measles outbreak. But the main driver is declining vaccination rates, which experts blame on the Trump administration, specifically HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr, as Scary Mommy previously reported.

Recent findings suggest that the CDC and American Academy of Pediatrics both recommend children get their first measles vaccine dose between 12 and 15 months of age, and the second dose between 4 and 6 years of age before starting school. According to CDC data, 96% of measles cases in 2026 have occurred in unvaccinated individuals. A KFF poll found that roughly one in five adults believe getting the measles vaccine is more dangerous than becoming infected with the measles. Parents are commonly exposed to vaccine misinformation, and data indicates it is affecting their health decisions: the number of kindergarteners with vaccine exemptions rose to 4.2% in the 2025-2026 school year, the highest in the country’s history, with 39 states falling below the 95% vaccinated threshold needed to prevent outbreaks.

Industry observers note that “The expected loss of America’s status as having eradicated measles will be a tragedy because it reflects the preventable loss of human lives. It is unthinkable that people in the United States should be dying from measles in 2026,” remarked Wendy S. Armstrong, M.D., president of the Infectious Diseases Society of America, in a publicly issued statement. “Our government’s leaders and public health officials must heed this urgent warning and take actions that slow the spread. That starts with promoting vaccination against measles, which is proven to be safe and effective.”.

Sources indicate that the largest outbreak in the U.S. since it earned measles elimination status, prior to the current one, was in 2018-2019. It was curtailed through a strong federal and state-level public health response, including closing schools where transmission occurred, prohibiting unvaccinated children from attending school, and fining parents for not vaccinating their children, KFF reports. The CDC also declared a public health emergency and made “clear statements about the importance of measles vaccinations.”.

But last week, CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz told Reuters that the agency will not make any major changes to their handling of the outbreak regardless of PAHO’s decision. The CDC will continue to “help [the states] provide awareness about ​measles, emphasizing, reemphasizing that the number one way to prevent measles is the MMR (combined measles, mumps and rubella) vaccine,” she stated.

She attributed the ongoing spread of measles to “closely knit communities” — several outbreaks have started in religious communities, like among the Pennsylvania Amish, where vaccination rates are lower than other parts of the country.

“These communities typically don’t vaccinate their children...their families were making decisions about the MMR vaccine 20 to 30 years ago and we’re just now seeing the results of those decisions,” Schwartz noted.

In response, the AAP and nearly 150 other health care organizations published a letter calling on Kennedy Jr. and Schwartz to develop and implement a plan to eliminate measles in the United States. Their recommendations include restoring evidence-based immunization policies, proactively encouraging measles vaccination, and conveying accurate information about measles and MMR vaccines.

This article was originally published on November 9, 2026.

  • Industry observers note that what’s great is that you can buy a lot more with it than just your basic bandages or the odd bottle of contact solution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bonus: They’re all literally proven to be good for you, too!

Recent findings suggest that here’s a fun fact about your Flexible Spending Account (FSA): whatever you don’t spend by the deadline is gone. Granted, some plans give you a little grace period or rollover a small amount, but most of us are on the use-it-or-lose-it clock. And while Health Savings Account (HSA) money doesn’t expire, it’s still sitting there earmarked for your health, and the holidays are a good excuse to finally use it.

Industry observers note that what’s great is that you can buy a lot more with it than just your basic bandages or the odd bottle of contact solution. We’re talking heating pads, period underwear, sunscreen, smart rings... even ergonomic office chairs can qualify! Some of the bigger-ticket items here (like the Lettuce Grow) may require a letter of medical necessity, but that typically just means filling out a quick online health questionnaire at checkout through a service like Truemed or Flex. Everything else you can usually just swipe your HSA/FSA card for. Of course, rules vary by proposal, so check yours if you’re not sure.

One notable caveat: HSA/FSA funds can only be used for you, your spouse, and your dependents. That means the following picks are perfect for treating yourself, stuffing your kids’ stockings, or, you know, finally getting your snoring partner something that’ll ultimately help you both sleep.

Here are some of our favorite items that are often covered by HSA and FSA guidelines.

If you know someone who gets painful period cramps or has endometriosis or adenomyosis, these little menstrual heat pads are such a thoughtful stocking stuffer. I stick them inside the waistband of my pants, and it genuinely gets hot enough to offer relief and go wherever I go all day. They last for hours, and I just love that they let me get relief without feeling stuck to a heating pad (and therefore a wall outlet). — Katie McPherson.

Industry observers note that isn’t it great when really trendy, great-smelling, cute beauty products are also good for you and eligible to buy with tax-exempt money? This is the case with Touchland hand sanitizer, which is all the rage with tweens and teens, and for good reason. It’s so cute and fun that it makes keeping germs away a blast. This is so perfect for stocking stuffing. — Sarah Aswell.

Recent findings suggest that as someone who works from home, I’ve always struggled with back pain from sitting hunched over a laptop all day long. I never even thought to check whether an office chair could be HSA/FSA-eligible... until I found out about Branch, which is usually through Truemed. Yes, you typically need to fill out a short form to get a letter of medical necessity, but it’s so worth it if the end result is a beautiful Branch office chair with 14 points of adjustment, including lumbar support that moves up, down, in and out, with armrests that adjust five ways. It’s also nice that there are so many upholstery options (I ordered the black boucle!). — Julie Sprankles.

Ancestry DNA Origins & Traits Kit.

Sources indicate that while not all DNA kits are eligible for HSA and FSA spending accounts, ones that give you health information are usually kosher. This one, from Ancestry, falls into that category. Have fun learning more about yourself and your past while also finding out medical information that could change your life. This is a great gift for someone who has everything. — Sarah Aswell.

According to recent reports, one of the most popular purchases with FSA and HSA money is this heated massage gun. It feels amazing, and it makes you feel better in the long run. We like this one because it gets killer reviews and comes with an app. Again, this is a major-ticket item that might turn out to be a great way to spend FSA money at the end of the year. — Sarah Aswell.

I have a chronic illness that causes high inflammation, so I tend to have a lot of body pain... especially in my joints. This flexible, wearable device combines red light, infrared light, micro-vibration, and micro-magnetic pulses in one band. I’ve found that if I strap it on to whatever aches, it really seems to help ease the pain. You should be able to pay directly with your HSA/FSA card, but it’s always a good idea to check with your specific health blueprint to see if you need a letter of medical necessity. — Julie Sprankles.

Industry observers note that supergoop is one of my favorite beauty products and by far my favorite sunscreen firm. They make my skin look and feel great while protecting it for the future. Many of Supergoop’s products are FSA- and HSA-eligible, including this mineral eye cream that works like a dream. But don’t sleep on many of their other products — I also love their Unseen Sunscreen for faces. — Sarah Aswell.

Geniani XL Electric Heating Pad Throw.

I am not exaggerating when I say that my life was changed by breaking down and getting an electric heating pad for my bed. It makes my sore body feel better, it prevents stiffness, and it is also just really, really nice when I have my period and I’m feeling crampy. — Sarah Aswell.

Recent findings suggest that this smart scale tracks 16 metrics, including muscle mass, body fat, and heart rate. You can pick the ones you want to show on the major color display and hide the rest, and it recognizes up to eight customers. Plus, it syncs up with Apple Health and Google Health. Oh, and it has a few fun extra modes: Baby Mode (in case you need to check before your next pediatrician visit), Pet Mode (if your pup is on a diet), and Luggage Mode (so you know before heading to the airport). — Julie Sprankles.

It has been revealed that I’m not proud of it, but in my middle age I’ve become a pretty bad snorer. The best gift I’ve ever gotten for my partner is these Ozlo earbuds, which can’t be beat. They are really comfortable to sleep in, and the white noise makes you catch your Zs like a baby. The price is a bit splurgy, but can you put a dollar sign on deep sleep, especially if you can put it on your HSA card? — Sarah Aswell.

VisoOne Blue Light Blocking Glasses.

Man, do some reading about blue light glasses, and you’ll see that they have virtually no downside — especially if you wear them at night while looking at screens. It’s probably the best thing you can buy for yourself under $20 that can help you feel better and get better sleep. And VisoOne has some really cute styles, too. — Sarah Aswell.

I’ve always wanted an Oura ring but held off because (a) I’m a mom and tend to buy everything for everyone else first and (b) this is more than I normally spend on myself. So I was pleasantly surprised to find out it’s HSA/FSA-eligible! The Oura Ring 4 looks like regular jewelry but tracks more than 50 metrics like sleep, stress, heart health, cycle, and more, which is hugely helpful always but especially when you’re in perimenopause like so many of us on the Scary Mommy team are. — Julie Sprankles.

Keep Going Travel Family First Aid Kit.

I love giving first-aid kits to people for the holidays, especially if someone has recently gotten a new car, moved into a new place, or had a new baby. We should really have more of these in more places — and my favorite one is this cute portable one by Keep Going. There are so many cute patterns, and it fits anywhere from your glove box to a tote to a diaper bag. — Sarah Aswell.

Saalt Hanky Panky Boy Short Period Underwear.

Sources indicate that I love period undies so much! They don’t leak, they’re good for the environment, and they will save you a significant amount of money over time. My favorite pair is these boy shorts from Saalt called Hanky Panky. They have great coverage while also still managing to be cute. Most, if not all, period panties are eligible to be purchased with your HSA or FSA! — Sarah Aswell.

Caring Mill Vapor Shower Tablets.

One of my favorite discoveries of 2025 was shower tablets — also known as shower steamers. You throw them onto the floor of the shower and, over the course of your rinse, they evaporate and let off fumes infused with essential oils. Certain types can help clear out your sinuses (peppermint) or relax you for bed (lavender). They’re fun and they have a purpose. I like these from Caring Mill, which is a brand specifically for people buying HSA and FSA items. — Sarah Aswell.

Neutrogena Pink Grapefruit Cleansing Wipes.

Industry observers note that these cleansing wipes are great for everything from removing grit and makeup at night to keeping in your purse for a little refresh during the day. And they smell divine! — Sarah Aswell.

According to recent reports, I’ve had my Lettuce Grow for over a year now, and it’s one of my most favorite things in our house! It’s like having your own personal salad bar. The Nook grows 20 plants under built-in grow lights, and they arrive pre-sprouted, so you’re harvesting about twice as fast as you would from seed. It's such a great option for families who want to get more greens on the table, and it’s HSA/FSA-eligible through Flex. — Julie Sprankles.

I’ve been putting pimple patches in my daughters’ holiday stockings for a few years now, but only recently have I tried them out and discovered that they actually work and are really awesome! Many of them qualify for HSA/FSA purchases, especially if they are medicated. I love these spot patches from Curology, which contain the active ingredient hydrocolloid. — Sarah Aswell.

Cure Hydrating Electrolyte Drink Mix.

According to recent reports, I was surprised to find that some hydration drink mixes are FSA- and HSA-approved. Which is great because sometimes when I’m feeling rundown, I just put one of these in a massive glass of water and feel so much better. — Sarah Aswell.

#160485. Menopause Is Hurting Women at Work. Something Has To Change.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (914 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Scarymommy ↗ Open Full Page

Menopause Is Hurting Women at Work. Something Has To Change.

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (914 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scarymommy

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here’s what women can actually do about it.
  • According to recent reports, I distinctly remember sitting in AP English class as a junior in high school with such horrible period cramps that it must've shown on my face.
  • It was the first time in my life that I hadn’t felt well and advocated for myself, albeit only after being nudged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brain fog, hot flashes, no sleep... and zero workplace support. Here’s what women can actually do about it.

According to recent reports, I distinctly remember sitting in AP English class as a junior in high school with such horrible period cramps that it must've shown on my face. I kept staring at the clock, and eventually, my very strict, no-nonsense teacher came to my desk and asked if I was OK.

“Can I go home early?” I asked.

It was the first time in my life that I hadn’t felt well and advocated for myself, albeit only after being nudged.

Then, in my 20s, I was severely nauseous with my first pregnancy but kept suffering through it at work because I wanted to save up my PTO for maternity leave. Now, I work from home, but as I’m hitting my late 30s, I wonder if I’d be any better at advocating for my needs in the workplace if I had perimenopause symptoms.

It has been revealed that truthfully, I’m not sure I would be — and I’m far from the only one. In a latest study, Womea surveyed more than 830 employed U.S. women ages 45 and older about how perimenopause or menopause symptoms affect their experiences at work.

Of those surveyed, 60% mentioned no one at work knew they were experiencing symptoms. Meanwhile, 90% said their employers have no menopause or midlife health policies in place. An alarming 87% said their symptoms affected their job performance in the past year, and 17% believed their symptoms cost them a promotion, raise, or high-visibility project.

In a recent development, so what’s a woman to do when she finds her perimenopause or menopause symptoms interfering with her career? And what can we reasonably expect our employers to do about it?

Industry observers note that perimenopause is the hormonal transition that leads us on the lovely path to menopause. It can begin in a woman’s 30s, although it more commonly starts in her 40s. “Fun” symptoms include brain fog, sleep disruption, mood changes, hot flashes, and irregular periods.

Dr. Gillian Goddard, a board-certified endocrinologist and author of The Hormone Loop, claims disrupted sleep can leave a woman feeling physically and mentally sluggish. Declining estrogen levels also affect dopamine activity, making it harder to concentrate. Research also suggests that learning new information can become more difficult during this period.

That helps explain why half of the women in the Womea survey reported experiencing brain fog or losing their train of thought during a meeting, client call, or presentation.

Women in this stage might not feel like themselves physically and emotionally, claims Lauren Tetenbaum, LCSW, JD, PMH-C, MSCP, a Newly introduced York-based women’s reproductive mental health expert and the author of Millennial Menopause: Preparing for Perimenopause, Menopause, and Life’s Next Period.

As a psychotherapist, Tetenbaum notes many of her clients are ambitious and dedicated to their careers, but are “caught off guard by the symptoms… they were never warned about.” Not even by their own healthcare providers!

Rather than recognizing that they may need medical care or additional rest, some women catastrophize what they’re going through, she states, worrying that brain fog could be a sign of early dementia or that they’re no longer capable of meeting their own high standards. “The performance is often not the issue; it’s the self-perception,” Tetenbaum says.

Still, it’s not easy for women navigating midlife at work.

Women can feel pushed out of the workforce during major life transitions, Tetenbaum notes, from matrescence to perimenopause, because they're presented with a false choice: “Sacrifice your health or wellbeing or values to work here, or leave, and don’t you dare show ‘weakness’ by asking for help.”.

We shouldn’t have to choose between our health and our careers... nor should we feel obligated to disclose personal medical details to our managers just to get support.

In a recent development, instead, Tetenbaum encourages women to familiarize themselves with their workplace benefits, such as health insurance coverage, PTO, and possible accommodations. (Sometimes, especially in competitive fields, employees can worry that taking PTO makes them look noncommitted. But taking care of ourselves shouldn't be seen as professional weakness. After all, we can’t bring our best selves to work if we're not feeling our best.).

Tetenbaum also strongly urges women to seek medical care rather than assume they have to push through their symptoms.

Employers have to do their part, too.

Sources indicate that goddard says several workplace conditions can make this phase of life more difficult for women, including insufficient restrooms, unpredictable or long hours, limited opportunities for breaks, and confined workspaces. Addressing some of these conditions could make a difference.

Employers can also review their health insurance policies to make sure menopause-related care is covered, such as menopause specialists, behavioral and psychological health care, and other relevant services, adds Tetenbaum, as well as look at ways to implement flexible schedules, remote work options, temperature controls, and uniforms that don’t exacerbate symptoms.

Industry observers note that of course, every individual and workplace is different. So employers should never be afraid to ask employees what would help them, she states.

As for women thinking about leaving their jobs or reducing their hours because of symptoms, Tetenbaum cautions, “Try not to make long-term decisions during a moment you feel overwhelmed.”.

Industry observers note that and the best decision we can make of all? Learning to advocate for our needs... in every stage of our careers and bodies.

Industry observers note that if you’re a parent who lives to visit the next national park on their must-see list — the kind everyone turns to when they need to borrow camping supplies, who has probably seriously considered #vanlife at least once — of course you’re leaning toward nature-inspired baby names for your new little one. Whether you live in an arid region or they’re your favorite places to visit, these desert baby names will remind you of golden sands and endless blue skies.

Mojave asters are perennial flowering shrubs covered in beautiful purple blooms. This is a beautiful name choice if you like the idea of an earthy girl name, but floral names often strike you as too feminine. It gets bonus points for also meaning “star” in Greek.

Industry observers note that A canyon is a deep, narrow valley with steep, rocky sides, and usually there is a river at the bottom that has carved all that rock away over time. It would make a strong boy’s name, and subtly remind him to persevere, like water against stone.

Joshua Tree National Park connects the Mojave and Colorado deserts, and is known for its iconic bristled trees. While many desert baby names feel a little woo woo and whimsical, Joshua is a classic that’ll fly under the radar when you need it to.

In a recent development, this name means “fire”, if you’re drawing from the Arabic roots, or “my light” if you’re referencing the Turkish version. Something about it gives cool girl, yet grounded, and all of its meanings tie back to the heat and brightness of the desert.

Do any of these names sound just right for your the fresh baby in your nature-loving family?

#160482. Tech Report: Your kid needs you to have hobbies outside of motherhood. Here’s why

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (899 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mother ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Your kid needs you to have hobbies outside of motherhood. Here’s why

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mother

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.
  • Sources indicate that A whistle blew.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Twenty-four years. That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.

Sources indicate that A whistle blew. The crowd hushed to silence. A monotone call came over the loudspeaker, “Swimmers, take your mark,” followed by a loud electronic beep that signaled the start of the race. I felt the cold rush of water overtake my body upon diving in. The neurons in my brain feverishly told my muscles to complete the strokes I’d learned decades before. In seconds, it was done. I finished the race.

Recent findings suggest that when I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids. My son, a competitive swimmer himself, looked at me and earnestly mentioned, “Wow, Mom. I’m proud of you.”.

It has been revealed that like most moms, I have a packed schedule. I work, parent, volunteer at school, shepherd my two kids to practices and social gatherings, throw meals together, walk the dog, and occasionally find a moment to breathe. But over the past couple of years, I watched my growing kids, now ages 12 and 9, discover and engage in passions that light them up. It left me wondering, why not me, too?

“A recurring theme in my practice is women feeling they’ve lost their individual identities somewhere between work, parenting, and meeting everyone else’s needs,” says Carly Snyder, a New York City–based reproductive and perinatal psychiatrist. “Part of my work involves helping women recognize that their own interests and needs are legitimate.”.

Research highlights a multitude of benefits earned by pursuing hobbies. Hobbyists often have wider social networks, improved mental health markers, and enhanced positive emotions.

According to recent reports, hobbies offer a particularly important lifeline for mothers, who often report losing themselves to the demanding needs of family life. That rings true for Kaitlyn Edington, an art educator and mom of two who recalls struggling after returning to work as a teacher following the birth of her first child. “I was so depleted,” Edington says. She spent her workdays teaching with short breaks to pump, often bringing her computer into her pumping room so she could catch up on work, then went home to full nights of infant care.

One day while scrolling on Instagram, Edington saw an artist posting images of her sketchbook paintings. “She changed my life,” Edington says. “Her sketchbook paintings were so loose and free, and she was encouraging people to draw everyday. I remember thinking, ‘If I have to pump two to three times a day, which I absolutely hate, why not pair it with something that I love?’” From then on, Edington sketched when she pumped, and ultimately developed a habit of daily sketching that she continues 10 years later.

No longer in the pumping phase of life, Edington ensures she gets time to sketch by waking up before her kids. “I hold the habit of waking up before my kids as sacred,” she indicates. “I need that time, when nobody needs me. It’s my emotional rest.”.

Science backs Edington’s belief that her hobby stabilizes her mental health. “Reengaging in meaningful, enjoyable activities can be therapeutically valuable,” Snyder claims. “Behavioral activation, an evidence-based treatment for depression, specifically emphasizes reconnecting with activities that provide pleasure, purpose, or a sense of accomplishment.”.

Snyder has three children, ages 19, 16, and 11, and throughout their lives she has maintained her dedication to skiing, cycling, yoga and running, completing a total of 19 marathons. She knows her kids benefit from her hobbies. Each time Snyder trains for an upcoming marathon, “[My kids] witness my commitment, discipline, setbacks, and perseverance,” she says. “Watching a parent pursue a hobby provides opportunities to observe persistence, emotional regulation, problem-solving, and enjoyment.”.

But those benefits are secondary to the impacts hobbies have on the women pursuing them. “I think we’ve become so accustomed to framing everything mothers do in terms of how it benefits their children,” Snyder indicates. “Women are entitled to happiness and fulfillment for their own sake.”.

It’s simply an added bonus that when mom is happy for mom’s sake, the benefits for her kids naturally follow, according to multiple studies linking a mother’s well-being with her child’s. Plus, kids also learn that all stages of adulthood, including those under the umbrella of parenting, can include personal fulfillment, curiosity, and growth.

According to recent reports, the best way to start a hobby is to let yourself reconnect with something you already love. I remembered how much joy I got out of competing in swim meets in high school, and I was eager to recreate that glee. Ask yourself, “What did I love when I was a kid or a young adult?”.

Industry observers note that your hobby doesn’t have to involve intense commitment. “Reading, gardening, dancing, listening to music, or simply spending time alone can be just as meaningful as running a marathon,” Snyder says.

Search online for local groups involved in the activity you want to pursue. Your local library may have resources to help you get started as well.

When you’re ready to commit, set realistic goals. Start by focusing on your hobby consistently for just 10-15 minutes per day. Showing up is the main goal.

“Motherhood should expand a woman’s identity, not erase it,” Snyder advises. Which hobby will help expand yours?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Appetizer options this easy might even tempt you to make more than one.

The trick is finding holiday apps that look impressive, tastes delicious, and don't require you to spend the entire party convincing everyone to try it — yes, we are talking about you, edible amputee appetizer. Bonus points if it can be made ahead of time, packed up without making a mess and transported without losing its appeal.

No matter where you’re headed this season, these appetizers are guaranteed to earn you a spot on the invite list next year.

If you’re looking for something that feels a little more sophisticated without requiring culinary school, try Damn Delicious’ asparagus and gruyere tart. Made with store-bought puff pastry, fresh asparagus, and Gruyere cheese, it’s baked until golden brown and the perfect blend of crispy and savory. All you need to do is slice it into squares to make it party-ready.

Leftovers? No problem. Put them to work in Family Fresh Meals’ sausage stuffing bites, which blend Italian sausage, stuffing, cheddar cheese, and dried cranberries. Don’t skip the tart-and-sweet cranberry dipping sauce that pulls this easy-to-execute app together.

You know that one person who always reveals up with something that looks like it belongs on a restaurant menu? This whipped ricotta with honey and truffle from The Stush Kitchen is how you become that person, and it takes all of five minutes to prepare — including the time it takes to assemble it upon arrival.

It has been revealed that is it even the holiday season if there isn’t some cranberry and brie involved? These cranberry brie bites from Feel Good Foodie are practically made for holiday entertaining. They’re also portioned individually, which means no one has to awkwardly cut into a giant cheese wheel appetizer while balancing a cocktail in their other hand and nodding their head in a conversation pretending they understood what someone just noted.

Recent findings suggest that every holiday spread needs something a little unexpected, and these fried pickle latkes with everything bagel ranch from What Jew Wanna Eat definitely deliver. Think crispy mini potato pancakes with a pickle tucked inside, served with a ranch dipping sauce that gets an extra punch of flavor from everything bagel seasoning.

Well Plated’s brie en croute takes things up a notch with buttery sautéed apples, toasted pecans, and a drizzle of honey tucked inside. It’s warm, gooey, and exactly the sort of thing people tend to gather around at a holiday party. This recipe is also make-ahead friendly, which is always a win when your holiday to-do list is already a mile long. Transport it in its baking dish and give it a quick warm-up at your destination if possible.

Sources indicate that if you want to make an appetizer that looks like you spent far more time on it than you actually did, consider Budget Bytes’ marinated cheese. Layers of cheese soak up a savory marinade made with olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon, garlic, and fresh herbs, while roasted red peppers add a festive pop of color. Serve it with a significant pile of crackers and let guests build their own bites. The best part? You can assemble the entire dish a full day ahead.

Sometimes you need to bring something a little more substantial than a cheese-and-cracker situation, you know? The Forked Spoon’s sweet and tangy cranberry meatballs are a fun (and easy) way to mix things up using frozen meatballs. The slow cooker does most of the heavy lifting, and the combination of sweet, tangy, and slightly spicy flavors makes these a crowd-pleaser.

According to recent reports, filled with a creamy mixture of shrimp, cream cheese, green onions, garlic, and a little ginger, Damn Delicious’ cream cheese wontons are the kind of appetizer that will have guests reaching for seconds. Pro tip: bring along a dipping sauce and you'll have a party snack that feels like a takeout favorite.

You don’t even have to turn on the oven to bring Princess Pinky Girl’s buffalo chicken pinwheels to life. This no-bake option comes together in less than 15 minutes using tortillas, rotisserie chicken, cream cheese, Frank’s Red Hot, and a few other pantry staples. They’re easy to pack in a covered container, look pretty on a platter, and can be made ahead of time. That’s what we call a holiday hosting win.

    This ‘unhinged’ advice for toddler moms is actually pretty genius

    💡 Key Takeaways
